selection_rationale: cand-A1b9 (Verifier-Guided LLM Generation) best balances novelty, falsifiability, operational relevance, and compute feasibility; it tests a concrete generate–validate–repair intervention with a paired design and deterministic verifier outcomes, and received a reviewer "pass" contingent on specified design repairs.
unresolved_uncertainties: Generalisability to production multi-vendor live networks and long-term operation (verifier coverage and real-device side-effects).
Degree to which iterative generate–validate–repair eliminates operationally critical semantic errors compared with deterministic verification plus human-in-the-loop.
Risk of overfitting generated repairs to verifier semantics (configs that pass verifier checks but introduce unmodeled side-effects).
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Pre-register a diverse, justified task set with explicit inclusion/exclusion rules and document digital-twin/verifier limitations.
Use multiple verifier configurations or cross-validate outputs with a second independent verifier to reduce single-verifier bias.
Add preregistered measurements for potential unmodeled side-effects (simulated side-channel checks or additional execution diagnostics) and report them.
Specify exact prompt templates, seeds, full model identifier, repair-prompt policy, and include explicit prompt-sanitization steps in the preregistration.
